acceptance: make comment-policy-strict either passes on a clean tree or its documented scope matches the files it actually enforces
context: Observed while verifying the #2614 develop merge: scripts/check_comment_policy.py --mode strict reports 531 violations across 6882 files, including vendored _sources/tpc-ds/PATCHES.md, tracked binaries under benchbox/_binaries, .github/workflows files, and .gitignore. The enforced gates (run_comment_policy.py --native-tests in CI, --staged pre-commit) do not cover these paths, so strict-mode output is advisory noise that cannot go green. Either scope strict mode to enforced paths or document that it is informational.
description: Check whether comment-policy-strict is meant to gate anything; if so, exclude vendored/binary/out-of-scope paths, else mark it informational so a red target does not confuse contributors.
